BH Assurance grows 2.5 times slower than its market

In 2025 the Tunisian insurance market grew by 11.4 %, BH Assurance by 4.5 %. The cheapest growth lever is the client base it already has.

Who BH Assurance serves. Individuals (personnes physiques) and companies (personnes morales), through agents and the BH Bank network. Life, motor, property, health, transport, engineering and liability lines.

Market grew 11.4 %, BH Assurance 4.5 %, so it loses share. Life is the fastest-growing line. Selling more to existing clients and keeping their contracts is the most profitable answer, which is exactly what our assistant targets.

Renewals chased by hand. Advisors track expiry dates and invoices manually, so contacts come late.

Knowledge buried in PDFs. Precise answers on guarantees and exclusions are slow and error-prone.

Opportunity: an agentic assistant that knows which product each client needs, decides when and how to contact them, writes a grounded and compliant message, and lets an advisor validate before anything is sent.

Each number comes from our EDA: 69 % mono-product companies, 320 contracts expiring in September 2025 with 12 unpaid, identical rider proposals for 284 clients. The opportunity statement leads to the architecture on the next slide.

Inherited prototype: the starting point we aim to improve

The component diagram and process flow of the existing repository. Our work adds an audited baseline and proposes redesigned models and orchestration.

Components: LangChain agent, Gemma 3n LLM, zero-shot intent classifier, ChromaDB, MongoDB, FastAPI opportunity API.

Process: unanswered message, intent detection, choice of sales strategy, RAG search, AI response, admin dashboard.

These are the diagrams of the repository we start from. It already chains intent detection, RAG and an LLM. What it lacked: documented objectives, a reproducible data pipeline, and a recommendation model that is not leaky, which we show later.

Motor dominates portfolios, and natural bundles already exist

60 % of companies hold a motor product; motor, multi-risk professional and health are often held together, which a recommender can learn.

60 %

Left: products by number of companies holding them. Right: co-ownership; 30 companies hold both motor products, 10 to 11 combine motor or health with the multi-risk professional policy. These co-occurrences are the signal our model uses.

The prototype score looked perfect because it was leaking the answer

Its AUC of 0.997 measured whether a candidate equals the product already held, not whether a client will buy a new one.

What we checked. Bought = 1 on exactly the rows where candidate_product == LIB_PRODUIT: 100 % of 1,842 rows.

Consequence. Owned candidates score 0.97 on average, others 0.06. The model separates "already held" from "not held", a question with no business value.

Decision. Drop score and Bought, rebuild an honest target: hide one product a company owns and ask the model to find it from the rest of its profile (slide 18).

100 %
of rows where the label is a copy of an input: the 0.997 measures nothing useful
This is our most important data-understanding finding. A near-perfect metric is a warning sign. After the fix, performance drops to realistic values, but now it measures something useful: finding a product the client does not have yet.

MODELING RULES

Preserve grain and history

Namespace PM / PP source identifiers.
Extraction date ≠ purchase date; no invented history.
Aggregate facts before joins to avoid double-counting.

All tables are proposed. CSV outputs are the current analytical layer. Snapshot trends require repeated extracts; document chunks stay in the retrieval store.

This is a fact constellation, not a claim that a warehouse is deployed. The PM extract is a portfolio/candidate table, so deduplicate to one observed company-product holding per snapshot; do not invent individual PM contracts. The PP extract has contract IDs and supports contract snapshots. Client identifiers are namespaced by source and PM/PP type; use a governed mapping before merging identities. Product and date dimensions are conformed. Snapshot date is the recorded extraction date, not a reconstructed purchase date. Contract guarantees use a unique bridge pair; aggregate before combining facts to avoid fan-out. Payment transactions and interaction events are future facts requiring additional history. Premium and revenue measures are not claimed from the current extracts. SCD type 2 for client attributes can be added once repeated extracts and reliable change tracking exist. Document text remains outside the dimensional warehouse, linked through governed product metadata.

PARALLEL DOCUMENT PATH · PROPOSED INTEGRATION

Product documentation → parse & chunk → embeddings / retrieval store → search_conditions

Keep document version, source and product mapping with each chunk. This path supports grounded drafting, separate from fact-table aggregation.

RAG / DSO3.2
Quality gate

Check schema, uniqueness, date validity and FK coverage; quarantine invalid records with reasons.

Repeatable loads

Use batch lineage, watermarks and idempotent keys; retain raw data for replay and reconciliation.

Leakage boundary

Use only data available at scoring time; fit learned preprocessing inside training folds. Imputation isolation remains to fix.

Read the pipeline from left to right. Existing evidence is file ingestion, raw retention, EDA and preparation, processed CSV exports and the evaluated notebook 04 baseline. Batch IDs, automated ingestion, quarantine handling, dimensional warehouse loads, serving integration and monitoring are proposed engineering extensions. Deterministic cleaning can be shared, but learned imputers, encoders and feature statistics belong inside training folds; the current pre-split imputation is an acknowledged limitation. For production, enforce point-in-time availability. Load dimensions before facts, validate foreign keys and reconcile source-to-target row counts at each grain. Retries should be idempotent. Client messages and agent outcomes flow into operational storage first, then into analytical event facts. Documents follow a separate parsing/chunking/indexing pipeline and are joined conceptually by product and document metadata. Scheduled refresh and controlled retraining are intended, not deployed.

Missing values and outliers are treated as business decisions

We impute only where a rule exists, keep "unknown" visible to the model, and never delete a valid long contract.

  • Hidden NaN: 'NON DEFINI', 'Non classé', 'Non défini' converted to missing before counting.
  • Rule 1: sector taken from companies with the same activity.
  • Rule 2: domain mapping, e.g. CLINIQUE to health sector (5 companies).
  • Rest: explicit UNKNOWN level plus a sector_imputed flag (52 companies have neither sector nor activity).
  • Dataset B, contract age: 29 contracts above the IQR fence of 9.5 years, 28 of them loan-linked death cover. Valid, so kept, flagged and log-scaled.
  • Dataset A, contract age: 0 for 90 % of contracts, so the IQR fence is 0. Clipping would erase everything; we binarise into has_history.
Point out that blind statistical rules would have been wrong twice: IQR would flag every non-zero age in A, and would delete valid 15-year loan insurance contracts in B.

All encoders live in src/features.py and are fitted inside each training fold. Learned imputation is currently fitted before splitting; history features need an availability audit.

Inside each of the 15 folds

Split companies 4/5 train, 1/5 testFit encoders and model on train companies onlyRank all products not held for each test episodeScore HitRate@k, NDCG, MRR, coverage
This removes the original direct target leakage but is still a reconstruction proxy. Twelve catalogue products have no positive examples or branch mapping. Encoders are fold-local; learned imputation is not yet fold-local. Contract-history inputs need an availability audit.

Modeling approach: rank the products a client does not hold yet

An advisor pitches at most three products; exact-product exclusion alone does not ensure cross-line diversification.

Framing

Multi-class "which product is hidden?" turned into a ranking over all products not held. Top-k is a candidate list for the proposed agent, subject to suitability review.

Metrics

HitRate@3 (main), HitRate@1, NDCG@3, MRR; long-tail HitRate@3 on products beyond the 3 best-sellers; coverage of the catalogue.

Validation

5-fold GroupKFold by company, repeated 3 times (15 folds). Mean ± std; paired bootstrap resamples whole companies after averaging CV repeats.

Model ladder, from rules to learning

RulePopularitybest-sellers not held, what a generic campaign does
RuleSegment popularitybest-sellers of the client's category
RecommenderItem co-occurrenceclients holding X also hold Y
MLLogistic regressionmultinomial, profile + portfolio
MLRandom forestnon-linear sector × portfolio
MLGradient boostingstand-in for the prototype's CatBoost
We evaluate like a recommender, not like a classifier: what matters is whether the right product appears in the three the agent will propose. Grouped CV guarantees that a company is never in train and test at the same time.

First results: similar overall accuracy, three times better on the long tail

Learned models recover more long-tail products; future cross-selling effectiveness remains to be measured.

0.686 vs 0.654
HitRate@3, logistic regression vs popularity. Gain +3.2 pts; company-bootstrap 95 % CI +0.1 to +6.5. Small, conditional gain.
0.33 vs 0.11
long-tail HitRate@3. Gain +22.2 pts; company-bootstrap 95 % CI +15.8 to +29.6 (137 companies).
17 vs 7
distinct products ever recommended: the model personalises, popularity repeats.

Below targets: 0.686 / 0.329 vs 0.70 / 0.40. Intervals are conditional on current preprocessing and the selected model.

Paired bootstrap now resamples companies after averaging each episode over three CV repeats. Overall gain: +3.2 points, 95% CI +0.1 to +6.5 across 299 companies; long-tail: +22.2 points, CI +15.8 to +29.6 across 137 companies. The overall interval narrowly excludes zero, but the result is conditional on the selected model and preprocessing. It is not evidence of conversion uplift; fully fold-local imputation and temporal validation remain future work.

Local tool demonstration; integrated agent workflow proposed

Schema and real local output are demonstrated. Agent calls, grounded drafts and advisor integration are future work.

1

Trigger. New conversation, renewal date, or the client asks what else is offered.

2

Decide. The agent chooses the recommend action from the intent and context.

3

Call recommend_products(client_id, k=3).

4

Ground. RAG fetches the general conditions of the top product.

5

Draft. Gemma 3n writes a personalised pitch.

6

Validate. An advisor approves or edits; the outcome is logged.
